clue.text: Scant regard from redhead in a mini-dress

indicators.note: in means the head of red is set inside the phrase for the little frock

parts.note: a shift is a loose dress, and a mini is a short one
the head, or first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: A girl with red hair in a very short dress is treated dismissively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside SHORT SHIFT, between the H and the I of SHIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Short shrift means curt, dismissive treatment, little attention or consideration.

clue.text: Instrument needed to get sherry cask raised

parts.note: sack is an old name for dry sherry, as drunk by Falstaff

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word for a cask is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tub is a barrel or cask

explanation.surface: A musician needs to lift a barrel of sherry before playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TUB into BUT, placed below SACK in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is an early form of trombone, a Renaissance brass instrument.

clue.text: Some of the morris men made a bloomer

indicators.note: some of means only a portion of the letters of the phrase is taken

explanation.surface: One of the folk dancers made a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across mORRIS. 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flowering plant here; MORRIS men are English folk dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a kind of iris, a flowering plant, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Irritable about one Scotsman giving evidence

indicators.note: about means the word for irritable goes round the other pieces

parts.note: testy means short-tempered or irritable
I is the Roman numeral for one
mon is a Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered witness from Scotland takes the stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving evidence' is the definition, read as a noun phrase meaning the evidence given; MON is the Scots form of man.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony is the sworn statement a witness offers in court.

clue.text: Chief man is on active duty

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the word for man sits above the letters for active duty

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
AD is the abbreviation for active duty

explanation.surface: The commanding officer is serving at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a leader or principal, the person in charge.

clue.text: Grand declaration by a working model

definitions.meaning: impressive, stately in size or manner
a model at work might say she is striking a pose, split as I'M and a word for posing

explanation.surface: A model at work announces she is magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing describes something impressive and stately; split up, it is what a sitting model would say she is doing.

clue.text: Parsimonious drunk

explanation.surface: A miser who is also inebriated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight means both mean with money and intoxicated in colloquial English.

clue.text: Inviting glance pleased onlooker

parts.note: glad means pleased or happy
an eye is one that looks on, a watcher

explanation.surface: A happy spectator gives a come-hither look.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the glad eye is to look at them flirtatiously.

clue.text: Unconcerned because treatment costs nothing

parts.note: care is treatment, as in medical care
free means at no cost

explanation.surface: A patient is untroubled because the doctor charges nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means without worries or anxieties.

clue.text: Cheat high churchman of keen intellect

parts.note: a cardinal is a senior churchman, abbreviated CARD
sharp means quick-witted or keen

explanation.surface: A clever cardinal turns out to be a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who cheats at card games.

clue.text: Fruit in Antigua varies by the season

indicators.note: in means the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Caribbean produce changes with the time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across antiGUA VAries; 'by the season' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The guava is a tropical fruit with pink or white flesh.

clue.text: Bishop has stylish leather boot

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
U stands for upper-class, hence stylish or refined
skin, the hide of an animal, is what leather is made from

explanation.surface: A clergyman wears fashionable leather footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leather boot' reads as one phrase, but 'leather' is wordplay and 'boot' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A buskin is a calf-high boot, worn by actors in ancient Greek tragedy.

clue.text: Satire we misconstrued, so to speak

indicators.note: misconstrued means the letters of the two words are taken the wrong way and rearranged

explanation.surface: Readers misunderstood the satire, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were is a phrase meaning in a way, figuratively.

clue.text: Inclination to get T-shirt of the highest quality

parts.note: a tip is a tilt or slope
a T-shirt is a top, a garment for the upper body

explanation.surface: A preference for a shirt of first-rate quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop means excellent, first-rate.

clue.text: Guiding rule for Arctic and Antarctic sailor

parts.note: the Arctic and Antarctic are the earth's two poles
tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A navigator's principle for polar voyages.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a pole star is a guiding principle, as the North Star once guided navigators.

clue.text: As the boss, I name the price

parts.note: a charge is the price asked for something

explanation.surface: A manager announces that they set the cost.
explanation.definitionFit: In charge means having control, being the one in command.

clue.text: Make no move to detain whisky manufacturer

parts.note: to hold someone is to detain them
a still is the apparatus that distils whisky

explanation.surface: Arresting a distiller.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold still is to stay motionless.

clue.text: He uses articles to study the area around Ur

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
Sumer was the ancient region of Mesopotamia containing the city of Ur

explanation.surface: An archaeologist uses items to research ancient Mesopotamia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests grammar or artefacts, but it means goods bought and used.
explanation.definitionFit: A consumer is a person who buys and uses goods.

clue.text: Rough but otherwise excellent lad

parts.note: bully is an old word for excellent, as in bully for you
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A youth who is coarse but otherwise splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but otherwise' hints that BULLY has another, older sense here: excellent, not tormenting.
explanation.definitionFit: A bully-boy is a tough or thug, hence the attributive sense rough and intimidating.

clue.text: Constant flak causes local fury

parts.note: in Britain the local is one's nearby pub, a bar
rage means fury

explanation.surface: Neighbourhood anger produces sustained criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British word for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a continuous bombardment, of gunfire or criticism.

clue.text: Customer has right to property in Connecticut

indicators.note: in means the word for a legal claim is put inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut
a lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A buyer has a legal claim on land in a New England state.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone who uses the services of a professional, a customer.

clue.text: Shouted when therapy was applied

definitions.meaning: in informal use, to shout someone is to buy them a drink or meal

explanation.surface: Someone yelled while undergoing treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shouted' is not about yelling: in Australian and British slang to shout a round is to pay for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated covers both paying for another's food or drink and receiving medical care.

clue.text: Impatient order to be more active

definitions.meaning: a command to take less repose, split as two words

explanation.surface: An impatient command to stop lazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means fidgety and unsettled; split in two it is an instruction to relax less.

clue.text: Plant bringing a fortune to you and me

parts.note: a lot is a large amount, a fortune
us is the pronoun for you and me

explanation.surface: A flower brings us luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is an aquatic flowering plant.

clue.text: English country property

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A rural English holding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country property' reads as one phrase, but 'country' is wordplay and 'property' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large area of land and buildings owned by one person.

clue.text: Ismaili leader at home once more

parts.note: the Aga Khan is the spiritual leader of the Ismaili Muslims
in means at home

explanation.surface: The religious leader is home again.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means a second time, anew.

clue.text: Reflective woman?

indicators.note: reflective means the name mirrors itself, reading the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A thoughtful lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' seems to mean thoughtful, but it means the name is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Expect a delay

parts.note: to wait is to hold back or delay

explanation.surface: Anticipate a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to look forward to it or anticipate it.

clue.text: Self-confessed recidivist who lives on charity

definitions.meaning: a repeat offender admitting they cannot reform might say ...
a beggar who depends on alms

explanation.surface: A repeat offender who admits it lives off handouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is a beggar; split up, the word is the confession of one who cannot reform.

clue.text: Simplified procedures for dealing with derailments

indicators.note: procedures for dealing with suggests the letters of the next word are handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Railway accident protocols have been made more efficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Streamlined means made simpler and more efficient.
